pr_title: Execute shard snapshot tasks in shard-id order
pr_body:
Today within a single snapshot we execute tasks in an undefined order,
which can lead to a high level of WIP that must be repeated if shard
snapshots are paused for node shutdown. This commit adds an extra
comparator to sort the tasks according to their shard ID to ensure we
focus on completing ongoing shard snapshots ahead of starting new ones.

Closes #108739
pr_comments: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> It could be thousands of shards in a new snapshot request that we prioritize starting up instead of running file uploads for an older snapshot.

Nono we sort by snapshot start time first in any case, we're only talking here about the priority of tasks within a single snapshot.

> Nono we sort by snapshot start time first in any case, we're only talking here about the priority of tasks within a single snapshot.

Oh, right. Then we'd still be starting possibly thousands of shard snapshots, within the same overall snapshot, and we'd need to interrupt them all for shutdown regardless of progress? I'm not familiar with the mechanics of each particular step, so maybe that's cheap (no network calls) to do and irrelevant.
When interrupted I think it'd be the almost exactly the same amount of work either way.

issue_context.title: Limit shard snapshot work-in-progress
issue_context.body:
The pause-on-shutdown mechanism introduced in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/101717 in fact resets every affected shard-level snapshot such that they retry again from the beginning on their new node(s), discarding the work-in-progress uploads of each shard. Today we make no attempt to limit the amount of work-in-progress that might be discarded on a node shutdown, since we interleave the uploads of the files from every shard that is being snapshotted. This can mean that the discarded work can be very substantial (in one case we observed it to set the overall snapshot progress back by over 10TiB).

We should find some way to limit this WIP, focussing on completing individual shard snapshots sooner, to reduce the effects of a shutdown mid-snapshot.
comments: Kinda related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/89826 except that IMO there's no real need to _limit_ the number of pending shard snapshots, we just need to schedule them more intelligently.

I think this might have quite a simple fix. We're ordering the shard snapshot tasks thusly:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/b99025433a0451549a6b2ae9b5e892e794d9d922/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/repositories/blobstore/ShardSnapshotTaskRunner.java#L42-L44

Note that we're prioritizing tasks from the longest-running snapshot, but disregarding the shard to which those tasks pertain. If we added a shard-specific comparator to that chain then I think we'd achieve what we want here.

review_comments:
Could you point me at the code where this happens? And is it the case that starting the shard snapshots AFTER finishing uploading files won't be noop shard snapshots?

I'm mostly thinking about the cases where later snapshots complete shard snapshots even if the older snapshots aren't done. It'd be nice to know for sure that those later ones aren't ever doing work.

> Could you point me at the code where this happens?

What happens exactly? The code that prefers to start new shard snapshots over uploading files is the line that sorts by `SnapshotTask::priority`.

> I'm mostly thinking about the cases where later snapshots complete shard snapshots even if the older snapshots aren't done. It'd be nice to know for sure that those later ones aren't ever doing work.

I mean they could be doing work occasionally, if e.g. there are 10 threads and 9 of them are doing the last 9 tasks for an older snapshot, the free thread will start on the next task in the queue for the newer snapshot.

Sorry, I was burying the purpose of my questions. The point I was trying to get at is whether prioritizing new shard snapshots is best, instead of prioritizing file uploads and the completion of existing shard snapshots.

It doesn't seem obvious that the next snapshot of a shard will be a noop, whenever it gets scheduled, sooner vs later, because it could already have been a while since the first snapshot of that shard started.
I wonder if it would be better to prioritize finishing file uploads of existing shard snapshots. Focus on getting one good overall snapshot, not spreading resources out to other snapshots.
Yeah that's ok, we run one task to start the shard snapshot but then all its file upload tasks get queued up behind other earlier shards' work.

> I wonder if it would be better to prioritize finishing file uploads of existing shard snapshots.

AFAICT it doesn't matter, or at least there are fairly balanced pros and cons either way. The `ShardSnapshotTask` tasks are much more lightweight than the `FileSnapshotTask` ones so they don't meaningfully add to the WIP we're interested in limiting in this PR; meanwhile it'll save work overall to run them sooner.

It could be thousands of shards in a new snapshot request that we prioritize starting up instead of running file uploads for an older snapshot.

We don't have any stats on this edge case, though, and the behavior in unchanged by this patch, so seems fine to go forward with 👍
Where does the index-name order come in? I don't see it in COMPARATOR 🤔
